why: a=0.25 already holds the general commit/box part (i) but not the math-specific checking part (ii), and the hard-328 gap is in long problems that need (ii), so it recovers only ~12 of the 42-problem gap over base+cue 164 instead of the two-thirds share it gets on MATH-500.
Code-RL shares only the non-math commit part (i) and lacks the math-specific check-before-stop habit (ii), which is what the hard-328 long problems need, so it sits just above base+cue 164.
Code-RL at ~173/328 against RL plain 206 leaves the part-(ii) gap of about 33 problems, roughly -10 points, unlike the near-parity on MATH-500.

Code-RL carries the commit habit without the checking habit, so it stops earlier than both base+cue and RL (9,300-9,350 tokens) on long problems, about the 0.85 ratio it shows on MATH-500 (3,336 vs 3,944).
